note: The 30 items proposed as neutral-plausible, stripped to premise and hypothesis. No label, no author rationale, no sibling members, no domain — nothing that could anchor a second reading.

items.premise: The bakery on Wren Street opened its doors at five every morning through the winter of 2019.
items.hypothesis: The Wren Street bakery still opens at five in the morning.

items.premise: Nadia handed in her thesis on the last Friday of March, a full two weeks before her department's deadline.
items.hypothesis: Nadia had been working on that thesis for more than a year.

items.premise: Until last April the ferry to Kestrel Island ran twice a day; since then it has run on Saturdays only.
items.hypothesis: The twice-daily crossing to Kestrel Island had been running for many years before it was cut back.

items.premise: Theo and Ruth Okonkwo are siblings who grew up in the same house in Leeds; Ruth is four years older than Theo.
items.hypothesis: Theo and Ruth have the same mother and the same father.

items.premise: For eleven years Dolores Marchetti lived next door to the Farrells, and she looked after their cat whenever they went away.
items.hypothesis: Dolores Marchetti and the Farrells were friends.

items.premise: Ingrid Vance wrote to her old schoolteacher, Mr. Osei, every Christmas for twenty years, and he wrote back each time.
items.hypothesis: Ingrid Vance and Mr. Osei met in person at least once during those twenty years.

items.premise: The watercolours hanging in the hallway were painted by Amira Delacroix, who marks her work with a small blue heron.
items.hypothesis: Amira Delacroix paints professionally.

items.premise: The crime novels published under the name Rowan Ash were all written by Beatriz Alonso, a retired magistrate from Seville.
items.hypothesis: Beatriz Alonso drew on her years on the bench when she wrote those novels.

items.premise: The runner who crossed the line first in the Saltcoats ten-mile was Priya Raman; her twin sister Meena came ninth.
items.hypothesis: The two Raman sisters are often mistaken for one another at races.

items.premise: Since 2021 Devon Achebe has run the scheduling desk at the Northgate dental clinic, although he has no clinical training of any kind.
items.hypothesis: Devon Achebe answers to the clinic's senior dentist.

items.premise: Hannah Wexler directs the Barrow Vale community choir: she picks the programme each season and takes the Tuesday rehearsals.
items.hypothesis: Hannah Wexler stands in front of the Barrow Vale choir at its concerts.

items.premise: On the Ellisfield bridge project, Marta Kubik was the foreman who signed off each day's concrete pours.
items.hypothesis: Marta Kubik was the most senior person on the Ellisfield site.

items.premise: Since he retired, Gerald Vance has swum at the lido on Mondays and Thursdays.
items.hypothesis: Gerald Vance goes to the lido on no days other than Mondays and Thursdays.

items.premise: The Okarie family has kept a vegetable stall at the Thursday market in Ashcombe for six years, missing only the weeks when the market itself was cancelled.
items.hypothesis: The Okaries also sell their vegetables at markets in other towns.

items.premise: Dr. Solveig Haugen is called out at night perhaps three or four times a month, usually to the farms north of the village.
items.hypothesis: Dr. Haugen is the only doctor serving the farms north of the village.

items.premise: The Brennans put their house on Calder Road up for sale in September, hoping to settle nearer their daughter in Cork.
items.hypothesis: The Brennans have since moved to Cork.

items.premise: Tomás Iglesias applied for the joinery apprenticeship at Hallward & Sons because he wants a workshop of his own one day.
items.hypothesis: Hallward & Sons gave Tomás the apprenticeship.

items.premise: Miriam Stanek drafted a long letter of complaint to the water company, meaning to send it once she had collected her neighbours' signatures.
items.hypothesis: The letter reached the water company in the end.

items.premise: Ayo Bankole was visibly nervous before he gave the graduation address, stopping twice to steady his hands.
items.hypothesis: Ayo Bankole felt relieved once the address was behind him.

items.premise: When her old collie died in February, Frances Doyle gave up her usual walks along the towpath.
items.hypothesis: Frances Doyle was grieving for the collie.

items.premise: Karel Novak laughed and wept at once when his brother came through into the arrivals hall at Ostrava after eleven years abroad.
items.hypothesis: Karel Novak had been counting the days until his brother came home.

items.premise: Paula Ferreira joined the Kettlebridge rowing club in 2018 and still pays her subscription every January.
items.hypothesis: Paula Ferreira rows with the Kettlebridge club most weekends.

items.premise: Every driver at the Arden depot except two belongs to the transport union.
items.hypothesis: The transport union bargains over pay on behalf of the Arden drivers.

items.premise: The Thursday book group at Milford library has nine members, one of them Owen Blaise, who has been with it since it began in 2005.
items.hypothesis: Owen Blaise founded the Milford book group.

items.premise: The basement of the Alderney Hotel flooded after a water main burst under the street outside during January's cold snap.
items.hypothesis: It was the cold that made the water main burst.

items.premise: The Tiverton orchard lost most of its apple crop that year; a late frost in May had killed the blossom.
items.hypothesis: The Tiverton orchard finished that year out of pocket.

items.premise: The fire in the trawler's engine room started when a fuel line chafed through where it ran against a bracket.
items.hypothesis: The fuel line had been run incorrectly when the engine was installed.

items.premise: At six, Jonah Whitlock could not get through a sentence unaided; by the end of the following year he was working his way through chapter books on his own.
items.hypothesis: Jonah Whitlock was given extra help with his reading during that year.

items.premise: Marrowfield was a village of four hundred people in 1970; today some nine thousand live there and the old lanes have disappeared under new estates.
items.hypothesis: Most of Marrowfield's growth came from people moving out of the nearby city.

items.premise: After the accident Sefton Mbeki could not stand without help; eight months later he walked the length of the hospital corridor on his own.
items.hypothesis: Sefton Mbeki made a full recovery from his injuries.
